assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and was a landmark of detector-driven discovery. The 2013 prize recognised the theory, so the measurement itself remains unrecognised. The two general-purpose detectors, ATLAS and CMS, were independent and gave a clean, redundant confirmation. As an instrumentalist I weigh heavily the conception and construction of detectors able to find a particle in enormous backgrounds.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was made by thousands of people. The foundational contributions are the conception and leadership of ATLAS and CMS, so I propose the founding ATLAS spokesperson (Jenni), the founding CMS spokesperson (Della Negra) and the CMS project leader (Virdee). Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of the announcement and is a defensible alternative, so the balance among these names is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Discovery in 2012, with a decade of coupling and mass measurements consistent with the Standard Model. Recognition is fully mature, and the work is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Any experimental-collaboration prize raises the question of whether three individuals can fairly represent a collaboration; I cannot independently verify the precise roles of each credited person.
Whether the committee prefers to honour the detector builders or the analysis leaders at announcement time is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised controllable many-body quantum systems, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, Fermi-Hubbard physics and single-site quantum gas microscopy. The impact spans condensed matter, AMO and quantum information, and the experiments gave new quantitative access to strongly correlated matter.
assessment.attribution: The longlist credits five names covering theory (Cirac, Zoller) and experiment. A prize for the experimental realisations would fit Bloch (lattice experiments and the Mott transition), Greiner (Mott insulator and the quantum gas microscope) and Esslinger (fermionic Mott insulator and lattice Fermi gases). The theory proposals of Zoller and Cirac are the intellectual origin and form a separate candidate, so the split between theory and experiment is unresolved. The Mott transition work involved other groups, including Hänsch, whom I cannot verify here.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent confirmation by many groups; quantum gas microscopy and simulation of Hubbard models are now routine. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with candidate B011 (theory) and with the 2001 BEC prize; the committee may consider a combined or sequential recognition.
Priority among the 2002 to 2010 experiments is partly contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube built a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice and established high-energy astrophysical neutrinos as a new messenger: the diffuse flux, the TXS 0506+056 association, the Galactic plane and NGC 1068. This is a rare case of astroparticle instrumentation creating a new observational window, and it is close to my own field, so I am aware of potential bias and have tried to apply the same standard as to other candidates.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and the earlier AMANDA concept; Spiering was a central figure in the Baikal and AMANDA/IceCube programmes. The ideas of detecting neutrinos in natural media involve earlier pioneers, including Markov, Roberts and the DUMAND group, which limits a two-person allocation. Others in the collaboration were also essential.
assessment.maturity: Discovery in 2013, source evidence from 2017 and 2022 to 2023. The astrophysical interpretation is stabilising but individual source identifications still rest on a small number of objects, so the field is maturing rather than fully settled.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the milestones of 2017 and 2022 as sufficient confirmation.
Allocation of credit relative to the Baikal, DUMAND and KM3NeT precursors and the collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength idea, brought clocks to the 1e-18 fractional uncertainty level, opening relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and prospects for redefining the second. It is a clear case of precision measurement leading to new physical reach.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept and Ye led the demonstration of record precision, which is a natural and compact two-person attribution. Contributions from Hall, Hänsch and others related to combs are already recognised in 2005, and Ido and Kimble among others contributed early.
assessment.maturity: Many independent clock comparisons and international clock networks confirm the performance. Recognition is timely, although the redefinition of the second has not yet occurred.
uncertainties: Whether attribution is fully captured by two people or needs a third such as a theorist or the Sr-clock rival groups.
Relation to the 2012 prize on quantum control of single ions and to the 2005 comb prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states opened the twistronics and moire quantum-matter field with an extremely broad programme following. Impact on experimental practice is large and rapid.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators observed the correlated and superconducting phases in 2018. The three named people form a theory-plus-experiment prize configuration, although Cory Dean's group and others also made central contributions that are not on this list.
assessment.maturity: First observations date from 2018 and reproduction by several groups is established, but the mechanism of superconductivity is not settled, which makes it somewhat early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and phase diagram remain debated.
Neglected contributors to the experimental realisation, for example hBN-based devices or other groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED reached the strong-coupling regime for single microwave photons and superconducting artificial atoms, and it is the architecture underlying present superconducting quantum processors. Impact on quantum technology and fundamental quantum optics is very high.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposal (Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and colleagues, 2004) and the experiment (Wallraff et al.) are well documented, and the three named people are a fair configuration though Wallraff is absent from the list. Credit must also be set against Nakamura, Devoret and others.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories; however the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits is recent, and the committee may prefer to wait to avoid close succession.
uncertainties: Whether the experimental co-discoverer should be included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: SASE X-ray free-electron lasers deliver femtosecond, extremely bright coherent X-ray pulses and have transformed structural dynamics, imaging and warm dense matter. The achievement combined accelerator physics with photon science and has been broadly adopted at LCLS, SACLA and European XFEL.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini, Kim and Rossbach are credited here. The SASE concept has roots with Kondratenko and Saldin, Bonifacio, Pellegrini and Narducci, which the credited list does not capture. I selected the names offered but note the attribution is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Operating facilities since 2009 give strong independent confirmation, and the scientific use is mature.
uncertainties: Priority issues for the original SASE theory and the first experimental demonstrations.
Whether the facility builders such as Emma at LCLS should be considered; they are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping and precision measurement of antihydrogen and antiprotons test CPT symmetry and the matter-antimatter asymmetry at high precision, with ALPHA's spectroscopy and the gravity measurement being notable. As an antimatter experimentalist I appreciate the technical difficulty, but I treat the claim on its merits.
assessment.attribution: Gabrielse (precision trapping, antiproton and positron work, ATRAP) and Hangst (ALPHA antihydrogen trapping and spectroscopy) are plausible joint laureates, but Hangst's and ALPHA's results are collaborative and others such as Doyle, Wineland-like trap techniques and the ATHENA team are also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Sustained results over two decades; precision is improving, but no deviation from CPT has been found, so the long-term significance is still developing.
uncertainties: Absence of a discrepancy limits interpretive impact so far.
Priority in antihydrogen production and trapping among ATHENA, ATRAP and ALPHA.
